title: Regulations.gov (API v4)
agency: General Services Administration (eRulemaking Program), for participating federal agencies
questions: how many public comments did a proposed rule receive
proposed rules open for comment at EPA
dockets an agency opened this year
comments on a docket over time

key_only: more than about 10 requests an hour (DEMO_KEY limit); a free key allows 1,000 an hour

manual.how: Open each link in INSTRUCTIONS.md in a browser (they carry the public DEMO_KEY, about 10 requests an hour; put your own api.data.gov key in its place for more) and save the JSON under the given name; or search on https://www.regulations.gov, open the docket's 'Browse Comments' or 'Browse Documents' list, use 'Download' (CSV export of up to the first results), and upload the file.

cache.why: Dockets gain documents and comments daily; data/ is reused within a run.

redistribution.why: Federal agency documents and the metadata are U.S. government works (17 U.S.C. 105). Public submissions are posted as received: attachments can contain third-party copyrighted material and personal information the submitter chose to include; share counts and metadata, and quote comment text sparingly.

notices: Public comments on Regulations.gov are posted by the agencies as received; posted counts can differ from comments received (agencies may withhold duplicates, mass-mail campaigns or sensitive submissions).
citation: Regulations.gov API v4 (eRulemaking Program, GSA), {dataset}, api.regulations.gov, retrieved {retrieved_long}.
clarify: Comments posted or comments received? The API counts posted comments only; agencies may post a sample or one copy of a mass-mail campaign.
Which document or docket? Comments filed on a docket (filter[docketId]) include every document in it; on one document use filter[commentOnId] with its objectId.
